title: Multielement profiles of Vespula germanica and Vespa crabro (Hymenoptera: Vespidae) nests
content:
Abstract
Colony-derived matrices may retain information on elements incorporated during nest construction and could provide noninvasive materials for environmental characterization. This study investigated the multielement composition of nests of the German wasp, Vespula germanica (Fabricius, 1793), and the European hornet, Vespa crabro (Linnaeus, 1758), collected from a single rural site. Seven wasp nests and the base, 10 comb levels, and outer envelope (OE) of one hornet nest were analyzed for 31 elements using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICPMS). The 7 V. germanica nests showed substantial among-nest variation, while the V. crabro nest exhibited component-specific heterogeneity. Descriptively, many elements occurred at higher concentrations in the wasp nests than in the hornet nest components, although their multielement profiles overlapped considerably. Within-class principal component analysis further resolved variation among the 7 wasp nests and among hornet nest components, with the nest base, L10, and OE grouping relatively closely. To our knowledge, this is the first broad quantitative characterization of elemental variation among V. germanica nests and across successive structural components of a V. crabro nest using ICPMS. These findings also support the further evaluation of abandoned vespid nest material as a noninvasive, colony-derived matrix for multielement profiling and terrestrial environmental monitoring. Validation across additional independent nests, sites, and pollution gradients, together with characterization of construction materials and parallel analysis of environmental matrices, is required before its suitability for biomonitoring can be established.
